verdicts.note: Raw PDF pulled by curl (HTTP 200, 5.3 MB) and extracted with pdftotext -layout. The size checkbox row carries all three bands; footer reads TM & © 2024 Wizards of the Coast LLC, and the page is a photocopiable handout. Every limb (WotC, 2024, handout, size banded by population, village up to 500) is on the page.
Same raw PDF text; second checkbox of the size row, en dash as quoted. Exact string match.
Same raw PDF text; third checkbox of the size row. Exact string match.

verdicts.trueWording: “DEFINING TRAIT” — third element, after SETTLEMENT NAME and the size row
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: opens with — DEFINING TRAIT is not the handout's first slot
verdicts.note: Quote is on the page verbatim as the first large boxed field, but the tracker's field order is SETTLEMENT NAME, then the VILLAGE/TOWN/CITY checkbox row, then DEFINING TRAIT. The claim's own page note ('first field') is therefore wrong; DEFINING TRAIT is the first descriptive prompt, not the first slot.
Same raw PDF text; the boxed field immediately below DEFINING TRAIT. Claim asserts only that the slot exists and is so labelled — supported.

Same raw PDF text; fourth boxed field (after CURRENT CALAMITY). It is the only leadership-labelled slot on the sheet — the other fields are DEFINING TRAIT, CLAIM TO FAME, CURRENT CALAMITY, NOTEWORTHY PEOPLE/PLACES and the gp line — so 'single leadership slot' holds.
Same raw PDF text; a seven-line list column headed NOTEWORTHY PLACES sits beside a separate seven-line NOTEWORTHY PEOPLE column, so both the list-slot limb and the separation limb are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: “GP VALUE OF THE MOST EXPENSIVE ITEM FOR SALE”
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF text; the footer field above the copyright line. The whole sheet was read: the only other numerals are the population bands (demographic, not economic), so 'the only economic figure' holds.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: a simile drawn from its own building stock — the simile's image is tombstones, not the village's buildings
verdicts.note: Raw PDF (media.wizards.com, HTTP 200, 62 MB) via curl + pdftotext. The boxed read-aloud after 'Once they reach the village, read:' begins 'The gravel road leads to a village, its tall houses dark as tombstones.' Road, village and absence of any statistic are all supported; the simile's vehicle is tombstones (grave markers), while the houses are its subject, so 'drawn from its own building stock' is not what the page does.

verdicts.trueWording: “Death House is the name given to an old row house”
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the name the locals give it — the page never says locals bestow the name
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, 'History' section. The sentence continues 'in the village of Barovia (area E7 on the village map)'; naming by neither owner nor street address is supported (the Durst family is named only later), but the agent of the naming is unstated — the only 'locals' sentence on the page is 'Locals give the building a wide berth for fear of antagonizing the evil spirits'.

verdicts.trueWording: “provide a template for creating NPCs and building settlements”
verdicts.note: Raw HTML pulled by curl with a browser UA (HTTP 200, 323 KB), tags stripped locally — no summarizer. Byline 'by Mike Bernier', dated Nov 12, 2024 (launch day: the page carries 'The 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide is Now Available'), section heading 'Adventures, Handouts, and Ready-to-Play Maps'. Sentence: 'the handouts sprinkled throughout the book provide a template for creating NPCs and building settlements.'

verdicts.trueWording: “it replaces all rules in the 2014 version of the book”
verdicts.note: Raw HTML by curl with browser UA (HTTP 200, 270 KB), tags stripped locally. Under heading 'Using This Book with Older Books': 'When you play D&D with the Dungeon Master's Guide (2024), it replaces all rules in the 2014 version of the book.' Byline 'by DND Staff', Feb 20, 2025, tagged Studio Blog, on the WotC-owned D&D Beyond (page footer: Wizards of the Coast LLC | All Rights Reserved), so the publisher-attribution limb holds.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: in one sentence — the trade is in the next sentence, not the opener
verdicts.note: Raw HTML by curl with browser UA (HTTP 200, 284 KB), tags stripped locally. Under 'The Village of Icehaven' the opening sentence gives name, population and demographics and ends '—on the northern coast of the Dwendalian Empire.' The trade limb comes only in the following sentence: 'the people of Icehaven primarily ply their trades on fishing boats.' Free, official D&D Beyond Encounter of the Week column confirmed by the page's own tags.

Same raw article; the section heading is literally 'The Village of Icehaven'. The band limb is checked against the other raw source in this chunk: the 2024 Settlement Tracker's middle checkbox reads TOWN (POP. 501–5,000), so 5,000 falls in the town band while the column calls it a village. Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: “The leader of the village, Starosta Ernath Noack”
verdicts.note: Same raw article, under the heading 'Arrival of the Infected One' as the claim's page note says. Order is office title (starosta, the Dwendalian village-elder office — the page also uses 'Starosta of Icehaven' and 'the village starosta'), given name Ernath, surname Noack.
